endorsements.quote: Instead, institutions must therefore establish governance mechanisms that complement individual efforts, including: (a) an AI ethics committee comprising faculty, trainees, ethicists, and IT security experts; (b) mandatory error reporting systems; (c) regular policy reviews; and (d) clear protocols for auditing AI tools before introduction into educational or clinical settings ( 43 ).
Policy and governance Develop clear institutional usage policies; establish an AI ethics oversight committee Ensure consistent, responsible use; address gaps in accountability
Transparency and accountability Publish institutional guidelines; establish clear liability frameworks for AI-related errors Build trust and clarify responsibility
No AI generated output should be accepted without critical human evaluation ( 37 ).

AI literacy curricula for psychiatric learners should include: (a) understanding how LLMs work, including their statistical rather than symbolic reasoning nature; (b) recognizing typical failure modes, including hallucinations, biases, and sycophancy; (c) practicing critical evaluation of AI outputs against authoritative sources; and (d) identifying situations where AI should not be used at all.
Data governance Vetting of all AI platforms for HIPAA/FERPA compliance; prohibit input of identifiable patient data into unsecured tools Protect patient and learner confidentiality
Education and training Mandate AI literacy training for all learners and faculty; integrate critical evaluation skills into existing curricula Equip trainees to use AI safely and effectively

Clinical integration Require human in the loop protocols for any AI tool used in training contexts; prohibit unsupervised AI in patient facing assessments Prevent over reliance and erosion of clinical judgment
structured review, where supervisors periodically examine learners’ AI interaction logs

unlisted_practices: Require learners to justify inclusion or exclusion of each item in AI-generated differential diagnosis lists based on patient history and mental status examination.
Establish emergency override protocols for situations where AI generates potentially harmful recommendations.
Do not use AI chatbots as a replacement for traditional mental health support or professional supervision for learners; treat them only as an adjunct.
Prioritize and fund rigorous outcome-evaluation research on AI's educational impact, bias mitigation, and safety protocols.
Adopt a staged evaluation model (bench testing, pilot feasibility, clinical efficacy testing) so learners encounter only chatbots meeting safety and efficacy standards before patient-facing use.
Publish institutional AI guidelines openly and review them annually, involving learners in the review.
Train supervisors to recognize patterns of AI use at each learner level.
Use structured frameworks such as DEFT-AI to scaffold critical thinking during learner AI interactions.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/commentary article proposing a balanced framework and institutional recommendations for integrating generative AI into psychiatric education.
